definition: Merriam-Webster's Word of the Day for November 25, 2026 is: arbiter &#149; \AHR-buh-ter\&nbsp; &#149; noun An arbiter is a person with power to decide a dispute, or a person or agency whose judgment or opinion is considered authoritative. // The mayor will act as the final arbiter in any disputes between board members. // He is regarded as an arbiter of taste in the world of musical theater. See the entry > Examples: "Oscar documentary favorites are starting to emerge as critics and other arbiters begin to announce their nominees and shortlists, bringing some clarity to a wide-open awards race." — Matthew Carey, Deadline , 20 Oct. 2026
did_you_know: ? There's no disputing the origins of arbiter : it traces back to a Latin noun, with the same spelling, referring to an eyewitness, onlooker, or person appointed to settle a dispute. Several English words having to do with judging or being a judge stem from the Latin arbiter , including arbitration , which refers to the act of judging, and especially the hearing and determination of a disputed case by an arbiter. Arbitrary , in its oldest English usage, described things that depended on choice or discretion particularly regarding the decision of a judge or a tribunal. Arbitrator functions as a synonym of arbiter , though it tends to be the preferred term for legal situations whereas arbiter is more likely to appear outside of the courtroom, as in "music critics and other arbiters of pop culture taste."
